title: veritas-insurance-regression-and-signoff-playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook captures the Veritas Insurance customer-specific eval and regression plan for the claims summarization and policy Q&A features. It is intended to be the source-of-truth for acceptance criteria, the pinned prompt set used during CI/regressions, private dataset sampling/splits, and the sign-off checklist required before Dedicated/Private rollout.

High-level goals:
- Ensure model updates do not regress on critical safety and accuracy metrics for claims summarization and policy-answer generation.
- Provide deterministic pinned prompts for nightly regression and pre-release smoke checks.
- Define absolute and relative thresholds for pass/fail decisions and automated rollback triggers.

Customer context:
Veritas uses the model for two primary flows: (1) automated claims summarization (structured summary + severity estimation) and (2) policy Q&A (short factual answers referring to policy text). Both flows are latency-sensitive (95th percentile < 420ms for short queries in Dedicated) and require very low hallucination for regulatory reasons.

Pinned prompt set (CI/regression canonical prompts) - use exact text below for deterministic checks:
1) SUMMARY-CHECK-1:
"""System: You are an assistant that extracts a concise insurance claim summary. Include claimant, incident date, primary damage, estimated severity (low/medium/high), and whether immediate follow-up is required. Output as JSON with keys: claimant, date, damage, severity, follow_up_required.
User: Claim text: \"On 2025-03-12, John Milton slipped on an icy sidewalk outside 23 Pine Ave. He reported a sprained wrist and visible swelling. The claimant wants reimbursement for physical therapy and lost wages. No police report filed.\"
"""
Expected behavior: claimant=John Milton, date=", expected_date_placeholder (allow approximate ISO if exact not present), damage=sprained wrist, severity=low/medium, follow_up_required=yes/no.

2) POLICY-QA-1 (exact):
"""System: Answer the user using only the provided policy excerpt. If the policy does not contain the answer, reply 'INSUFFICIENT_INFO'. Do not invent clauses. Answer in 1-2 sentences.
User: Given policy excerpt: \"Section 4.2: Reimbursement for outpatient services covers physical therapy only when prescribed by a licensed physician within 30 days of incident. Dental claims for broken teeth are excluded.\"
Question: Is physical therapy covered if prescribed 45 days after an incident?\"""
Expected answer: INSUFFICIENT_INFO (or an explicit 'No, policy limits 30 days' if the excerpt is explicit).

3) HALLUCINATION-SMOKE-CASE:
Short prompt referencing invented entity to ensure model does not assert false sources.
"""System: Check whether the following claim references an actual police report and cite the report ID in the format REPORT_ID: ####.
User: \"Victim referred to police report PR-99988 in neighborhood file. Describe findings.\"
"""
Expected answer: The assistant should state it has no access to external reports and not fabricate a REPORT_ID; return 'NO_EXTERNAL_REPORT_ACCESS'.

Private dataset: veritas_claims_2023_v2.csv (encrypted, access restricted)\- Files and columns (summary):
  - claims_id (string)
  - claim_text (text)
  - incident_date (ISO)
  - claimant_name (redacted/encrypted in provided training subset)
  - policy_excerpt (text)
  - gold_summary (text) - human-annotated canonical summary
  - severity_label (low|medium|high)
  - allowed_answer (yes|no|insufficient)
  - reviewer_notes (text)

Dataset size and split:
- Full dataset: 28,742 claim rows collected calendar 2023.
- Shared eval slice used by CI (veritas_ci_slice.csv): 2,000 rows sampled stratified by severity and claim length.
- Regression smoke set: 120 hand-curated examples (includes edge cases, adversarial phrasing, redacted PII) used for nightly runs.

Data handling rules:
- All artifacts in this folder are PII-redacted and stored on the private customer vault. Any new sample added to the CI set must go through the privacy QA checklist (see linked_artifacts).
- When running local reproductions, use the provided stub credentials and do not export raw claim_text outside Redwood network.

Evaluation metrics and acceptance criteria (primary):
- Claims summarization (structured output): exact-key accuracy (JSON keys present and parseable) >= 98% on CI slice; field-wise F1 micro-avg >= 92% for claimant/date/damage; severity macro-F1 >= 88%.
- Policy Q&A: closed-book accuracy >= 95% on allowed/insufficient classification; factual precision (no hallucinated policy clauses) >= 98% as measured by human spot checks (sample n=200).
- Hallucination rate: measured by the specialized hallucination smoke set must be < 3% (where hallucination = any factually incorrect assertion not supported by input excerpt).
- Latency SLO for smoke tests (dedicated target): median < 220ms, p95 < 420ms when run against dedicated staging cluster.

Relative regression thresholds (pre-merge CI and post-deploy monitors):
- Any drop > 2 percentage points absolute in primary metrics vs. baseline model (baseline tag: veritas-baseline-2025-10-01) triggers a regression investigation.
- Hallucination increase > 0.5 percentage points triggers immediate canary hold.

Baseline and model variants:
- Baseline model: redwood-open-13B-qat@v2025-10-01 (evaluation numbers recorded in linked_artifacts).
- Allowable upgrade candidates: variants with quantization or kernel changes, but must pass full CI including the hallucination smoke set and latency checks.

Regression test procedure (CI and nightly):
1) Nightly deterministic run using pinned prompts (above) against veritas_ci_slice.csv with fixed RNG seed and sampling params (temperature 0.0 for determinism; top_p 1.0 if needed for non-generation tests).
2) Record and archive outputs in the veritas-evals S3 bucket with artifact id (date-run-model-hash).
3) Compute metrics and diff vs baseline; if any threshold breach, file JIRA with failure details and attach machine diff and 20 random failure examples.
4) Human-in-the-loop review for hallucination failures: sample 200 failures quarterly for fine-grained annotation.

Pre-release checklist (must be green before canary):
- [ ] Nightly regression: all pinned prompts pass acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Latency SLO tested against dedicated staging cluster at target load (50 concurrent small requests).
- [ ] Safety checks run (hallucination smoke set and policy-QA refusal behavior).
- [ ] Compatibility: KV cache and prefix caching validated on representative long-context cases (≥2048 tokens).
- [ ] Quantization profile validated (if applicable) with no more than 1% drop in field F1.

Canary and rollout plan:
- Canary 1: 5% traffic for 24 hours, telemetry hooks enabled for immediate rollback. Alerting: if any of the following occur, auto-rollback: 
   * absolute metric drop > 2 points in claims structured accuracy OR
   * hallucination rate > 4% OR
   * p95 latency exceed target by > 30%
- Canary 2: 25% traffic for 48 hours if Canary 1 passes.
- Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and sign-off.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Per-model per-route dashboards must show: token-level cost, latency p50/p95/p99, structured-extraction accuracy, hallucination spike chart, and per-prompt failure heatmap.
- Traces for failed requests must include request id, model commit hash, runtime kernel profile, and input prompt.

Sign-off owners and roles (required signatures):
- Applied ML owner (accuracy & regression): Aisha Patel
- Product owner (customer acceptance): Marisol Rivera
- Solutions/SE (deployment checklist): Liam Chen
- Customer success (contractual + go-live): Priya Menon

Sign-off checklist (final):
- [ ] All CI and nightly regressions passed on candidate model build.
- [ ] Privacy & compliance sign-off for dataset slice used in evals.
- [ ] SRE load test green on dedicated staging.
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards provisioned and alerts configured.
- [ ] Customer acceptance sign-off secured (email thread linked in linked_artifacts).

Appendix: quick-run commands for reproducing local evals (internal use)
- Run deterministic eval: python eval/run_eval.py --dataset veritas_ci_slice.csv --prompts pinned_prompts.json --seed 42 --sampling \"temp:0.0\" --model redwood-open-13B-qat@candidate
- Archive outputs: aws s3 cp outputs/ s3://veritas-evals/{date_run}_{model_hash}/ --recursive

Open questions / known risks:
- Edge-case coverage for extremely long police/medical attachments is limited in the current CI slice; plan to expand the regression smoke set with 40 long-doc examples next quarter.
- Need to finalize redaction rules for claimant_name in the training-to-eval handoff (privacy team pending).

Next steps:
1) Resolve privacy QA blockers (owner: Priya) — target 2025-11-22.
2) Run comprehensive latency sweep on dedicated staging (owner: Liam) — target 2025-11-20.
3) Customer review meeting to walk through acceptance metrics and sign-off criteria (owner: Marisol) — schedule week of 2025-11-24.

If you update this doc, add a one-line change log at the top and notify the collaborators channel.
